newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian soldiers, rebels play soccer in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russian soldiers, rebels play soccer in Chechnya.

text.p: Russian soldiers beat Chechen rebels 3-1 on Sunday in an unprecedented soccer match in the regional capital Grozny where fragile peace is holding after the withdrawal of troops and separatist forces.

Itar-Tass news agency said the pitch in Grozny, where the match between the St Petersburg OMON crack police squad and rebels of field commander Arbi Kurbanov took place, had first to be cleared of mines left by recent fierce fighting in the city.
Tass said the OMON servicemen and rebels, who fought each other in Grozny throughout 21 months of war, now formed a single group patrolling the city's Novopromyslovsky district.
Joint patrols were introduced after withdrawal of Russian and rebel forces from the city under the latest peace deal hammered out by Russian peacemaker Alexander Lebed and separatist leaders.

Tass quoted the players as saying they were ready to take part in a wider tournament in Chechnya -- its name, Lebed's Kubok Mira, may be translated as "Peace Cup" -- on condition that all other pitches are cleared of mines.
